chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated to us, who said: Harun ibn Muslim ibn Sa'dan narrated to us, from Mus'ada ibn Sadaqah al-Rub'i, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) who said:

For the believer upon the believer are seven obligatory rights from Allah, the Exalted: Honoring him in his sight, loving him in his chest, assisting him with his wealth, that he should deem for him what he deems good for himself, and that he should forbid backbiting him, and that he should visit him in his illness, and escort his funeral, and not speak of him after his death except good.
ai.seo_question: What are the seven rights of a believer over another believer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defining these seven rights as divine obligations, thereby elevating social etiquette to a matter of theological accountability. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on *mu'akhat* (brotherhood), linking internal sincerity—such as genuine love in the heart—with external actions like financial mutual aid and dignified conduct in death.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-28 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted Harun ibn Muslim ibn Sa’edan, on the authority of Mus’adat ibn Sadaqah al-Rub’ee, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), “The Honorable the Exalted God has established seven rights for each believer incumbent upon any other believer as follows:

1- He must honor him in his sight.2- He must love him wholeheartedly.3- He must help him.4- He should consider to be good for him whatever he considers to be good for himself and should not gossip about him.5- He should visit him when he gets ill.6- He should attend and escort his funeral procession.7- He should only speak good of him after his death.”
